Confidence intervals for drmTMB models and effective doses

Source: R/profile.R
confint.drmTMB.Rd

Profile likelihood intervals (default), Wald intervals, or parametric bootstrap intervals for the coefficients and variance parameters of a drmTMB model, or for effective doses estimated by ed.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'drmTMB'
confint(
  object,
  parm = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  method = c("profile", "wald", "boot"),
  nsim = 500,
  seed = NULL,
  boot = NULL,
  vcov. = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'edTMB'
confint(
  object,
  parm = NULL,
  level = if (identical(object$type, "bmd")) 0.9 else 0.95,
  method = c("profile", "wald", "boot"),
  nsim = 500,
  seed = NULL,
  boot = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a drmTMB or edTMB object

parm

parameters or effective doses, names or positions in coef(object); default all

level

the confidence level: 0.95 by default, and 0.90 for the benchmark doses of bmd, whose lower and upper limits of the two-sided 90% interval are the BMDL and BMDU of EFSA and the US EPA (as for bmdma and bmdbayes)

method

"profile" for profile likelihood intervals, "wald" for Wald intervals, or "boot" for percentile intervals of a parametric bootstrap: responses are simulated from the fitted model (with new random effects, see simulate.drmTMB) and the model is fitted again to each, starting at the estimates. Fits that do not converge are left out, with a message.

nsim

number of bootstrap simulations

seed

an optional seed for the random number generator of the bootstrap

boot

a bootstrap sample of the model from bootstrap, used instead of new simulations; implies method="boot"

vcov.

for drmTMB objects, the covariance of the estimated parameters for Wald intervals: a matrix as vcov() of the fit, or a function of the fit that returns one, e.g. the sandwich covariance vcovrobust; implies method="wald". Effective doses computed with vcov. (see ed) get Wald intervals by default.

...

further arguments passed to profile.drmTMB, profile.edTMB or bootstrap, e.g. progress=FALSE

Value

a matrix with the lower and upper confidence limits

Details

Standard deviations of the random effects, the residual standard deviation and the precision are reported on their natural scale; Wald intervals for them are computed on the log scale. The correlation of a term with two random effects is reported as a correlation; the parameters of larger correlation matrices on the unconstrained scale of coef.

For effective doses, peaks and benchmark doses, the available methods are:

  • profile: effective doses of the population curves (random=FALSE in ed, or models without random effects), peak doses, and BMDs that are not averaged over random effects (see bmd for the exceptions);

  • bootstrap: as profile, and also the curves of fitted groups (newdata in ed), with the random effects of the groups drawn from their conditional distribution at each bootstrap fit;

  • Wald only: effective doses with random=TRUE for random effect terms without a fitted group, or with residual=TRUE, and the response at a peak.

Where a method is not available, Wald intervals are returned with a message. Wald intervals of effective doses and BMDs are symmetric on the dose scale and can have negative lower limits; with small-sample inference (see drmTMB) they use t quantiles with n - p degrees of freedom. Bootstrap intervals need many fits of the model; with random effects this can take several minutes. Computing profiles can take a while for models with random effects; see profile.drmTMB and profile.edTMB, whose results can be reused with confint.

See also

profile.drmTMB, profile.edTMB, bootstrap, vcovrobust, ed, bmd

Examples

mod <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic",
              start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))
confint(mod)
#> Computing profile confidence intervals ...
#>                    2.5 %     97.5 %
#> b2:(Intercept)  7.436904  8.2868123
#> b3:(Intercept) -3.398753 -1.8910294
#> b4:(Intercept)  2.879209  3.7038016
#> sigma           0.405628  0.7178603
confint(mod, method = "wald")
#>                     2.5 %     97.5 %
#> b2:(Intercept)  7.4303933  8.2804619
#> b3:(Intercept) -3.1808940 -1.7597546
#> b4:(Intercept)  2.8549066  3.6718047
#> sigma           0.3958726  0.6970697
confint(ed(mod, respLev = 50), level = 0.9)
#> Computing profile confidence intervals ...
#>             5 %     95 %
#> 50:lf1 2.942286 3.622696
